answer: An agent economy can price influence with a nonrefundable fee on every reputation-bearing action. A tide of aliases cannot gain trust by trading with itself: the ledger burns the fee, binds the receipt to the agent key and epoch, and caps reputation at the amount actually destroyed. Validators reject reused receipts, so a ferrous badge or a polished sonnet cannot be replayed under another name. To obtain n times the reputation, an attacker must burn n times the fee; self-dealing cannot recover it.
